subject: Chemistry
question: In a laboratory flame test, Calcium salts ($\text{Ca}^{2+}$) impart which characteristic color to a non-luminous Bunsen flame?

options.A: Brick-Red (Orange-Red)

explanation: Calcium cations ($\text{Ca}^{2+}$) excite to produce a distinct brick-red (orange-red) flame coloration.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Precipitation Test for Fe(II) and Fe(III)
question: When aqueous Sodium Hydroxide ($\text{NaOH}$) is added dropwise to a solution of Iron(II) Sulfate ($\text{FeSO}_4$), the observation is:

options.A: A dirty green precipitate of $\text{Fe(OH)}_2$ forms, which turns reddish-brown on exposure to air
options.C: A chalky white precipitate soluble in excess $\text{NaOH}$

explanation: $\text{Fe}^{2+} + 2\text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{Fe(OH)}_2downarrow$ (dirty-green precipitate), which slowly oxidizes in air to reddish-brown $\text{Fe(OH)}_3$.

subject: Chemistry
question: When dilute Hydrochloric Acid is added to an unknown salt, effervescence occurs. The gas evolved turns clear Lime Water milky. This confirms the presence of:

options.A: Carbonate ($\text{CO}_3^{2-}$) or Hydrogencarbonate ($\text{HCO}_3^-$) anions

explanation: Carbonates react with acid to liberate $\text{CO}_2$ gas: $\text{CO}_2 + \text{Ca(OH)}_2 \rightarrow \text{CaCO}_3\downarrow + \text{H}_2\text{O}$, turning lime water milky.

subject: Chemistry
question: In a laboratory flame test, volatile salts of the Barium cation ($\text{Ba}^{2+}$) impart which characteristic color to the non-luminous Bunsen flame?

options.A: Apple Green (Pale Green)

explanation: Barium salts impart a distinctive apple green color to the flame due to characteristic electronic transitions in thermally excited barium atoms.

subject: Chemistry
question: When aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ is added dropwise to a solution containing $\text{Zn}^{2+}$ ions, a white precipitate forms that dissolves in excess $\text{NaOH}$ to give a colorless solution. This occurs because $\text{Zn(OH)}_2$ is:

options.A: Amphoteric, forming the soluble complex Tetrahydroxozincate ($\text{[Zn(OH)}_4]^{2-}$)

explanation: Zinc hydroxide is amphoteric: $\text{Zn(OH)}_2(s) + 2\text{OH}^-(aq) \rightarrow [\text{Zn(OH)}_4]^{2-}(aq)$ (soluble zincate complex).

subject: Chemistry
question: Which of the following is the standard laboratory confirmatory test for identifying alkaline Ammonia gas ($\text{NH}_3$)?

options.A: It turns damp red litmus paper blue and produces dense white fumes of $\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$ with a glass rod dipped in concentrated $\text{HCl}$
options.B: It relights a glowing wooden splint
options.C: It turns acidified potassium dichromate green
options.D: It gives a pop sound with a burning splinter

explanation: Ammonia is basic (turns red litmus blue) and reacts with $\text{HCl}$ vapors to form dense white airborne ammonium chloride smoke: $\text{NH}_3(g) + \text{HCl}(g) \rightarrow \text{NH}_4\text{Cl}(s)$.

subject: Chemistry
question: To test for Sulfate ions ($\text{SO}_4^{2-}$), the test solution is acidified with dilute $\text{HCl}$ before adding Barium Chloride ($\text{BaCl}_2$). Why is the addition of dilute $\text{HCl}$ mandatory?

options.A: To destroy and eliminate any interfering Carbonate ($\text{CO}_3^{2-}$) or Sulfite ($\text{SO}_3^{2-}$) ions that also form white barium precipitates
options.B: To speed up the evaporation of water
options.D: To change the color of barium ions to yellow

explanation: Barium carbonate ($\text{BaCO}_3$) also forms a white precipitate with $\text{Ba}^{2+}$, but decomposes in acid. Acidifying prevents false-positive carbonate interference.

subject: Chemistry
question: What is the simple laboratory confirmatory test for Oxygen gas ($\text{O}_2$)?

options.A: It relights a glowing wooden splint held at the mouth of the test tube

explanation: Oxygen supports vigorous combustion; introducing a glowing wooden splint causes it to burst immediately into a bright flame.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Testing for Sulfate Anion with Barium
question: When aqueous Barium Chloride ($\text{BaCl}_2$) is added to a test solution acidified with dilute $\text{HCl}$, the formation of which insoluble precipitate confirms the presence of Sulfate ions ($\text{SO}_4^{2-}$)?

options.A: A dense white precipitate of Barium Sulfate ($\text{BaSO}_4$)

explanation: $\text{Ba}^{2+}(aq) + \text{SO}_4^{2-}(aq) \rightarrow \text{BaSO}_4(s)\downarrow$ (white precipitate, insoluble in dilute mineral acids).

subject: Chemistry
question: Why is a platinum or nichrome wire cleaned repeatedly in concentrated Hydrochloric Acid ($\text{HCl}$) and heated in the flame prior to performing a flame test?

options.A: To convert any residual metal impurities into volatile metal chlorides that vaporize, cleaning the wire completely
options.B: To coat the wire with non-flammable diamond
options.C: To cool down the metal wire below room temperature
options.D: To dissolve the wire into liquid

explanation: Concentrated $\text{HCl}$ converts contaminant metal cations into volatile metal chlorides that vaporize off in the hot flame, ensuring the wire imparts zero baseline color.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Flame Test Colors - Strontium and Copper
question: In a laboratory flame test using a clean platinum wire, volatile salts of Strontium ($\text{Sr}^{2+}$) and Copper ($\text{Cu}^{2+}$) impart which characteristic flame colors respectively?

options.A: Crimson Red for $\text{Sr}^{2+}$, and Blue-Green for $\text{Cu}^{2+}$
options.B: Golden Yellow for $\text{Sr}^{2+}$, and Lilac for $\text{Cu}^{2+}$
options.C: Apple green for $\text{Sr}^{2+}$, and Brick red for $\text{Cu}^{2+}$

explanation: Strontium imparts an intense crimson red color to the flame, while copper halides impart a vibrant bluish-green coloration due to quantized electronic relaxation.

subject: Chemistry
question: When aqueous Magnesium Sulfate ($\text{MgSO}_4$) is added to a cold test solution, a white precipitate of $\text{MgCO}_3$ forms immediately in the cold with Carbonate ($\text{CO}_3^{2-}$), whereas with Hydrogen Carbonate ($\text{HCO}_3^-$):

options.A: No precipitate forms in the cold, but a white precipitate of $\text{MgCO}_3$ appears upon boiling the mixture
options.C: A black precipitate forms that dissolves in acid

explanation: Magnesium bicarbonate $\text{Mg(HCO}_3)_2$ is soluble in cold water. Boiling decomposes it: $\text{Mg(HCO}_3)_2 \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{MgCO}_3\downarrow + \text{CO}_2\uparrow + \text{H}_2\text{O}$.

subject: Chemistry
question: When acidified Silver Nitrate ($\text{AgNO}_3$) is added to an aqueous solution containing Bromide ions ($\text{Br}^-$), what precipitate is observed and what is its solubility in ammonia?

options.A: A pale cream precipitate of $\text{AgBr}$, which is sparingly / partially soluble in concentrated aqueous Ammonia ($\text{NH}_3$)
options.B: A pure white precipitate fully soluble in dilute ammonia
options.C: A canary yellow precipitate insoluble in concentrated ammonia

explanation: $\text{Ag}^+ + \text{Br}^- \rightarrow \text{AgBr}\downarrow$ (pale cream precipitate). $\text{AgBr}$ is sparingly soluble in concentrated aqueous ammonia, distinguishing it from $\text{AgCl}$ (soluble) and $\text{AgI}$ (insoluble).

subject: Chemistry
topic: Testing for Iron(III) Cation with Thiocyanate
question: When Potassium Thiocyanate ($\text{KSCN}$) solution is added to an aqueous sample containing Iron(III) ions ($\text{Fe}^{3+}$), what unmistakable diagnostic visual test occurs?

options.A: Formation of an intense blood-red coordination complex ($[\text{Fe(SCN)(H}_2\text{O)}_5]^{2+}$)

explanation: $\text{Fe}^{3+} + \text{SCN}^- \rightarrow [\text{Fe(SCN)}]^{2+}$. The thiocyanatoiron(III) complex exhibits an intense, diagnostic blood-red color sensitive to trace ferric ions.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Testing for Ammonium Cation with Nessler's Reagent
question: When Nessler's Reagent (alkaline potassium tetraiodomercurate(II), $\text{K}_2[\text{HgI}_4]$) is added to an aqueous solution containing Ammonium ions ($\text{NH}_4^+$), it gives:

options.A: A characteristic brown precipitate or rich yellow-brown coloration (Iodide of Millon's base)
options.B: A pure white precipitate soluble in water

explanation: Nessler's reagent reacts with ammonia/ammonium to precipitate the brown basic amino-mercuric complex $\text{HgO} \cdot \text{Hg(NH}_2)\text{I}$ (Iodide of Millon's base).

subject: Chemistry
question: When dilute aqueous Ammonia ($\text{NH}_3$) is added dropwise to a solution containing Copper(II) ions ($\text{Cu}^{2+}$), a light blue precipitate of $\text{Cu(OH)}_2$ forms initially, which upon adding excess ammonia:

options.A: Dissolves completely to form an intense deep royal blue solution of the tetraamminecopper(II) complex ($[\text{Cu(NH}_3)_4]^{2+}$)
options.B: Turns into solid black copper metal

explanation: $\text{Cu(OH)}_2(s) + 4\text{NH}_3(aq) \rightarrow [\text{Cu(NH}_3)_4]^{2+}(aq) + 2\text{OH}^-$. The formation of the soluble deep blue tetraammine complex confirms copper(II).

subject: Chemistry
question: When dilute Hydrochloric Acid is added to a solid metal sulfide sample, the evolved gas turns moist Lead(II) Acetate test paper to which color?

options.A: Shiny silvery-black or dark brown due to the formation of Lead(II) Sulfide ($\text{PbS}$)

explanation: Sulfide reacts with acid: $\text{S}^{2-} + 2\text{H}^+ \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{S}\uparrow$. Hydrogen sulfide gas reacts with lead acetate: $\text{H}_2\text{S} + \text{Pb(CH}_3\text{COO})_2 \rightarrow \text{PbS}\downarrow (\text{black}) + 2\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Amphoteric Hydroxide - Zinc Hydroxide with Excess NaOH
question: When aqueous Sodium Hydroxide ($\text{NaOH}$) is added dropwise to a solution of Zinc Sulfate ($\text{ZnSO}_4$), a gelatinous white precipitate of $\text{Zn(OH)}_2$ forms. Adding excess $\text{NaOH}$ causes the precipitate to:

options.A: Dissolve completely to form a clear colorless solution of Sodium Zincate ($[\text{Zn(OH)}_4]^{2-}$ / $\text{Na}_2\text{ZnO}_2$)
options.B: Turn into an insoluble red powder

explanation: Zinc hydroxide is amphoteric: $\text{Zn(OH)}_2(s) + 2\text{OH}^-(aq) \rightarrow [\text{Zn(OH)}_4]^{2-}(aq)$ (tetrahydroxozincate(II) ion), dissolving into a clear solution.

subject: Chemistry
question: Which simple chemical test paper confirms the evolution of greenish-yellow Chlorine gas ($\text{Cl}_2$)?

options.A: It bleaches moist blue litmus paper red initially, then completely white (bleaching action), and turns moist starch-iodide paper blue-black
options.B: It turns dry filter paper bright red
options.C: It turns lime water milky with no bleaching
options.D: It has no effect on any indicator paper

explanation: Chlorine oxidizes iodide to iodine in starch-iodide paper: $\text{Cl}_2 + 2\text{I}^- \rightarrow 2\text{Cl}^- + \text{I}_2$ (blue-black with starch) and bleaches dyes via hypochlorous acid ($\ext{HOCl}$).

subject: Chemistry
topic: Identification of Sulfur Dioxide Gas with Dichromate
question: Sulfur Dioxide gas ($\text{SO}_2$) is confirmed when it turns filter paper soaked in acidified Potassium Dichromate ($\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$) from:

options.A: Orange to Green (due to reduction of $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}$ to $\text{Cr}^{3+}$ ions)

explanation: $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7 (\text{orange}) + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 + 3\text{SO}_2 \rightarrow \text{Cr}_2(\text{SO}_4)_3 (\text{green}) + \text{K}_2\text{SO}_4 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$. Reduction to chromium(III) sulfate yields a green color.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Confirmatory Test for Nitrate Ion (Brown Ring Test Chemistry)
question: In the Brown Ring test for Nitrate ions ($\text{NO}_3^-$), what is the exact chemical composition of the dark brown coordination complex ring formed at the junction of the two liquid layers?

options.A: $[\text{Fe(H}_2\text{O)}_5(\text{NO})]^{2+}$ (Pentaaquanitrosyliron(II) sulfate complex)

explanation: $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ reduces $\text{NO}_3^-$ in presence of concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ to $\text{NO}$, which coordinates with hydrated iron(II) to form the brown ring $[\text{Fe(H}_2\text{O)}_5\text{NO}]^{2+}$.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Cobalt Glass in Flame Tests for Potassium
question: Why is a Cobalt Blue Glass filter held before the eye when performing a flame test on a mixture containing both Potassium and Sodium salts?

options.A: Cobalt blue glass completely absorbs the intense golden-yellow flame emission of Sodium ($589\text{ nm}$), allowing the faint lilac/violet flame of Potassium to be seen clearly
options.B: It protects eyes from ultraviolet rays
options.D: It cools down the flame temperature

explanation: Cobalt glass absorbs sodium's overwhelming yellow emission wavelength while transmitting potassium's violet/lilac light, enabling identification in mixed salts.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Amphoteric Zinc Cation (Zn2+) Reaction with Excess NaOH
question: When Sodium Hydroxide ($\text{NaOH}$) is added dropwise to a solution containing $\text{Zn}^{2+}$ ions, a white gelatinous precipitate forms which dissolves in excess $\text{NaOH}$ to give a clear colorless solution of:

options.A: Sodium Zincate ($\text{Na}_2[\text{Zn(OH)}_4]$ or $\text{Na}_2\text{ZnO}_2$)

explanation: $\text{Zn}^{2+} + 2\text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{Zn(OH)}_2\downarrow$ (white). In excess base: $\text{Zn(OH)}_2 + 2\text{OH}^- \rightarrow [\text{Zn(OH)}_4]^{2-}$ (soluble complex tetrahydroxozincate).

subject: Chemistry
question: What is the confirmatory test for Sulfate ions ($\text{SO}_4^{2-}$), and why is dilute Hydrochloric acid added beforehand?

options.A: Addition of aqueous $\text{BaCl}_2$ yields a thick white precipitate of $\text{BaSO}_4$ which is insoluble in dilute $\text{HCl}$ (preventing interference from carbonates/sulfites)

explanation: $\text{Ba}^{2+} + \text{SO}_4^{2-} \rightarrow \text{BaSO}_4\downarrow$ (white precipitate). Adding dilute $\text{HCl}$ decomposes and rules out carbonates and sulfites which also form white barium precipitates.

subject: Chemistry
question: When Ammonia gas ($\text{NH}_3$) or an Ammonium salt is treated with alkaline Nessler's Reagent ($K_2[\text{HgI}_4]$), what distinct observation confirms its presence?

options.A: A characteristic reddish-brown precipitate (Iodide of Millon's base) is formed
options.B: A bright blue solution is formed

explanation: Nessler's reagent ($K_2\text{HgI}_4$ in $\text{KOH}$) reacts with $\text{NH}_3$ to form a sensitive reddish-brown precipitate of Millon's base iodide ($\text{H}_2\text{N-Hg-O-Hg-I}$).

subject: Chemistry
topic: Halide Ion Precipitation with Aqueous Silver Nitrate (AgNO3)
question: When aqueous Silver Nitrate ($\text{AgNO}_3$) acidified with dilute $\text{HNO}_3$ is added to separate solutions of $\text{Cl}^-, \text{Br}^-$, and $\text{I}^-$, the precipitate colors observed are respectively:

options.A: White ($\text{AgCl}$), Cream / Pale Yellow ($\text{AgBr}$), and Bright Yellow ($\text{AgI}$)
options.C: All three form identical white precipitates

explanation: $\text{AgCl}$ is white (soluble in dilute $\text{NH}_3$), $\text{AgBr}$ is cream (soluble only in concentrated $\text{NH}_3$), and $\text{AgI}$ is bright yellow (insoluble in conc. $\text{NH}_3$).

subject: Chemistry
question: When aqueous Ammonia ($\text{NH}_4\text{OH}$) is added in excess to a light blue solution of $\text{Cu}^{2+}$ ions, the initial pale blue precipitate dissolves completely to form an intensely deep royal blue solution containing:

options.A: Tetraamminecopper(II) complex cation ($[\text{Cu(NH}_3)_4]^{2+}$)

explanation: $\text{Cu(OH)}_2(s) + 4\text{NH}_3(aq) \rightarrow [\text{Cu(NH}_3)_4]^{2+}(aq) + 2\text{OH}^-$. The coordinate complex $[\text{Cu(NH}_3)_4]^{2+}$ gives the characteristic deep royal blue color.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Hydrogen Sulfide Gas Rotten Egg Odor Test
question: Hydrogen Sulfide gas ($\text{H}_2\text{S}$), identified by its foul rotten-egg smell, turns filter paper moistened with Lead(II) acetate solution into what color?

options.A: Silvery-black or shiny brownish-black (due to precipitation of Lead(II) Sulfide, $\text{PbS}$)

explanation: $\text{H}_2\text{S}(g) + (\text{CH}_3\text{COO})_2\text{Pb}(aq) \rightarrow \text{PbS}\downarrow\text{ (black)} + 2\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$. This is the standard confirmatory test for sulfide gas.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Iron(II) vs Iron(III) Hydroxide Precipitate Colors
question: Addition of Sodium Hydroxide ($\text{NaOH}$) solution allows visual distinction between $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ and $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ cations because they form precipitates of:

options.A: Dirty green precipitate of $\text{Fe(OH)}_2$ for $\text{Fe}^{2+}$, and Reddish-brown precipitate of $\text{Fe(OH)}_3$ for $\text{Fe}^{3+}$

explanation: $\text{Fe}^{2+} + 2\text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{Fe(OH)}_2\downarrow$ (dirty green, turns brown in air). $\text{Fe}^{3+} + 3\text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{Fe(OH)}_3\downarrow$ (reddish-brown rust color).

subject: Chemistry
topic: Limewater Test for Carbon Dioxide Gas
question: When Carbon Dioxide gas is bubbled through clear Limewater ($\text{Ca(OH)}_2$), it turns milky white, but on prolonged bubbling the milkiness disappears because:

options.A: Insoluble Calcium Carbonate ($\text{CaCO}_3$) dissolves into soluble Calcium Hydrogen Carbonate ($\text{Ca(HCO}_3)_2$)

explanation: Initial milkiness: $\text{Ca(OH)}_2 + \text{CO}_2 \rightarrow \text{CaCO}_3\downarrow + \text{H}_2\text{O}$. Excess $\text{CO}_2$: $\text{CaCO}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{CO}_2 \rightarrow \text{Ca(HCO}_3)_2(aq)$ (soluble and clear).
